paper_title: DLP Dynamic Layerwise Pruning in Large Language Models
caption: Perplexity of LLaMA1-7B on different validation datasets under varying quantization bits.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: The figure presents three bar charts depicting the perplexity of the LLaMA1-7B model evaluated on different validation datasets: WikiText, PTB, and C4, each corresponding to varying quantization bits of 3, 4, 8, and 16. The horizontal axis represents the quantization bits and is labeled as such, showcasing a linear scale which increases in integer steps from 3 to 16. The vertical axis denotes perplexity, also labeled accordingly, with a range starting from 0 and extending to the maximum observed values in each chart. The scale intervals of the vertical axis differ between charts, with WikiText and C4 having intervals that appear to be evenly spaced up to around 30, while the PTB chart extends to 400. Each dataset features two bars per quantization bit: one for "Uniform" represented by blue bars and another for "Ours" represented by orange bars. The bars are arranged according to the quantization bit values. The charts also include a legend to differentiate the two datasets clearly, allowing for visual comparison of the perplexity values between the two methods at each quantization level. Specific values for perplexity can be inferred from the heights of the respective bars, with noticeable differences in performance across the quantization levels and datasets.
model_annotations.English: The presented figure consists of three bar charts labeled (a) WikiText, (b) PTB, and (c) C4, illustrating the perplexity of the LLaMA1-7B model across different validation datasets with varying quantization bits (3, 4, 8, and 16). The horizontal axis in each chart represents the quantization bits, while the vertical axis denotes perplexity, with values starting from 0 and extending to varying maximum values specific to each dataset—reaching around 30 for WikiText and C4, and up to approximately 400 for PTB. The bars in each chart are in two colors: blue represents "Uniform" and orange denotes "Ours." In the WikiText chart, the tallest bar is the blue one at 3 bits, which reaches close to 30 perplexity, while the orange bars remain lower, with maximum values around 25. In the PTB chart, the blue bar for 3 bits tops approximately 400, while the orange bar stays significantly below, with each of the subsequent quantization bits for both categories decreasing perplexity overall. Lastly, the C4 chart closely resembles the WikiText bar heights, but at lower values, with the uniform configuration showing slightly higher perplexity across all quantization levels than the “Ours” bars, although the difference is more pronounced at the lower quantization bits. Each bar grouping is organized by quantization bits in ascending order, and no specific bars are visually emphasized beyond the coloration representing the two configurations.
model_annotations.German: Das Diagramm besteht aus drei getrennten Balkendiagrammen, die die Perplexität des LLaMA1-7B-Modells auf verschiedenen Validierungsdatensätzen (WikiText, PTB und C4) in Abhängigkeit von der Anzahl der Quantisierungsbits darstellen. Die vertikale Achse zeigt die Perplexität an, während die horizontale Achse die Anzahl der Quantisierungsbits (3, 4, 8 und 16) auflistet. Die Balken sind in zwei Kategorien unterteilt: "Uniform" (blau) und "Ours" (orange). Im ersten Diagramm (WikiText) zeigt sich die Perplexität für beide Methoden, wobei die Werte für "Uniform" durchgehend höher sind, mit einem höchsten Wert von etwa 30 bei 3 Bits und einem niedrigeren Wert von rund 20 bei 16 Bits für "Ours". Das zweite Diagramm (PTB) hat deutlich höhere Werte, wobei die Perplexität für "Uniform" bei 3 Bits einen Wert von nahezu 400 erreicht. Auch hier sind die Werte für "Ours" durchgehend niedriger, ohne eine größere Abweichung im Verlauf. Im letzten Diagramm (C4) sind die Werte wieder niedriger, ähnlich dem ersten Diagramm, wobei auch hier die "Uniform"-Balken durchweg höher bleiben als die von "Ours". Alle Balken sind nicht sortiert und zeigen keine speziellen Hervorhebungen.
